title: ZigbeeZCL: Added 'raw value' items for UTC fields.
description:
The 'raw value' fields help with performing tshark checking in automated
test environments, independent of the formatted time. These are hidden fields
so, should not conflict with the associated UTC fields.

notes.body:
added 2 commits
  • 77b2487d - 1 commit from branch wireshark:master
  • b52020fd - ZigbeeZCL: Added 'raw value' items for UTC fields.
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/22465/diffs?diff_id=1577628559&start_sha=c7ddb12d006273f2cfcbdceecf089c588b48f793)

How are you using TShark in your automated test environment? What output of TShark are you parsing? There are ways to get the raw packet data that is used to add the time fields in TShark output already, with the PDML and with "json" with the "-x" option or the "jsonraw" output methods.

@johnthacker Thank you for the comment. An example of a tshark check looks as follows,

zbee_zcl.cmd.id == 0x01 && zbee_zcl.attr.status == 0x00 && zbee_zcl.attr.utc_raw == TESTTIME

Where, TESTTIME is a unsigned value instead of UTC time.

Please note that there is a precedance for this with the 'zbee_zcl.attr.utc_raw' which is currently supported by Wireshark.

And also many of the utc time fields for which I have added the 'raw' hidden items, used to look like as follows previously,

`        { &hf_zbee_zcl_price_start_time,
            { "Start Time", "zbee_zcl_se.price.start_time", FT_UINT32, BASE_CUSTOM,
                CF_FUNC(decode_zcl_se_utc_time), 0x00, NULL, HFILL } },`


whereas these are now updated as follows,

`        { &hf_zbee_zcl_price_start_time,
            { "Start Time", "zbee_zcl_se.price.start_time", FT_ABSOLUTE_TIME, ABSOLUTE_TIME_UTC,
                TIME_VALS(now_strings), 0x00, NULL, HFILL } },`

Which essentially breaks the checking that we used to perform.

Hope this answers your question.
Ah, so what you are saying is that your check involves filtering, I see

Have you tried filtering with the @ operator?: https://www.wireshark.org/docs/wsug_html_chunked/ChWorkBuildDisplayFilterSection.html#_the_at_operator

It should work for any field without having to add a new hidden field.
You would have to take into account that the bytes are little endian
ok, thanks for the inputs. I will look into this.
